questions.q: What does ethos refer to among Aristotle's modes of persuasion?
a: The speaker's credibility and authority on the topic
The emotional connection with the audience
The data and evidence behind the argument
The overall structure of the presentation
questions.why: Lesson 1 traces ethos to the speaker's standing and the trust their expertise earns.

questions.q: What mix does Gallo call the perfect talk?
a: 65% pathos, 25% logos and 10% ethos
65% logos, 25% pathos and 10% ethos
Equal parts pathos, logos and ethos
50% pathos, 40% ethos and 10% logos
questions.why: Lesson 1 says emotion should dominate, with data second and credibility a small slice.

questions.q: Whose talk featured a swim in open water and a child he feared was drowning?
a: Scott Dinsmore
Bill Gates
Joe Smith
Carmine Gallo
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses Dinsmore's swim, where he feared a child was drowning, as an extreme moment.

questions.q: How did Joe Smith make his paper towel statistic memorable?
a: He showed that one fewer towel a day would save half a billion pounds a year
He handed out samples of recycled paper towels
He compared paper towels with reusable cloths
He folded a sheet of paper enough times to reach the moon
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a familiar habit scaled up to a huge number makes the point stick.

questions.q: Why does Gallo recommend covering only three topics?
a: People remember information in about three chunks
Audiences lose interest after ten minutes
Three topics fill exactly eighteen minutes
Speakers can only prepare three stories well
questions.why: Lesson 3 says research now puts our working memory at roughly three chunks, not seven.
